subject.title: Feature: Inject context window % into system prompt runtime section

question: Should OpenClaw expose passive context-window usage in the system-prompt Runtime line, and what exact freshness and display contract should it use?
rationale: The source path is clear, but adding volatile per-turn prompt metadata changes model-facing prompt semantics and cache behavior, so automation should not choose percentage-only versus raw tokens, stale-snapshot handling, or model-switch behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve bounded Runtime field
options.body: Add `context=NN%` from fresh session total/context tokens, omit it when unknown or stale, keep it below the stable cache boundary, and leave raw details to status/session tools.

options.title: Keep explicit inspection only
options.body: Leave context usage on /context, /status, session_status, and diagnostics surfaces, then close or update this issue once maintainers decide passive prompt metadata is not desired.

options.title: Defer to runtime self-context design
options.body: Keep this issue dependent on the broader runtime self-awareness work instead of landing a narrow Runtime-line primitive now.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Runtime field
recommendation.body: Add `context=NN%` from fresh session total/context tokens, omit it when unknown or stale, keep it below the stable cache boundary, and leave raw details to status/session tools.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest available routing match for the prompt/runtime contract from current and earlier history.
